steps.title: Look at the verbs.
steps.prompt: What do we add to a regular verb to talk about the past?
steps.why: Regular verbs take -ed. The form is the same for every person.
steps.html:
I work every day. → I worked yesterday.

We live here now. → We lived there in 2015.

She studies English. → She studied English at school.

steps.title: Past Simple · regular verbs
steps.html:
PersonPositiveNegative
I / YouI worked late.I didn't work late.
He / She / ItShe called me.She didn't call me.
We / TheyThey waited outside.They didn't wait outside.

The past form is the same for every person. No -s after he or she.

Spelling: live → lived, stop → stopped, study → studied.

After didn't the verb goes back to its base form: didn't work, not didn't worked.

Verbs that do not take -ed come in Lesson 3.

steps.title: Spelling
steps.html:
The verb ends in…RuleExample
a consonantadd -edwork → worked
-eadd -dmove → moved
consonant + -y-y becomes -iedstudy → studied
one vowel + one consonantdouble the consonantstop → stopped
